To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the gill epithelion of shore crabs is leaky to NaCl, but the gill epithelial of freshwater adapted Chinese crab is moderately tight to NaCl.

the gills of shore crabs absorb Na+ and Cl- in a coupled mode via a cotransport-like mechanism, while the gills of Chinese crabs absorb Na+, but not Cl-, via a Na+-dependent, Cl−-independent mechanism.

shore crabs adapted for brackish water absorb NaCl via cotransport-like mechanisms, and freshwater adapted crabs absorb Na+ via apical Na+ channels and H+-pumps, and Cl− via apical Cl-/HCO3-exchange and Cl− channels.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how crabs can cope with a change from marine to freshwater.
the elucidation of transport mechanisms in the gill epitheliam and their functional significance with respect to the osmoregulatory strategy of shore crabs and freshwater-adapted crabs.
the elucidation of the mechanisms of salt uptake by the gill epitheliam and the adaptation of the shore crab to the freshwater environment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
freshwater-adapted crabs have overcome the osmotic stress in freshwater by a combination of Na+-dependent and Na+-indepentent Cl− uptake mechanisms.
the gills of Chinese crabs are equipped with a sophisticated mechanism for active ion uptake, and that this mechanism is able to overcome osmotic stresses in a freshwater environment.
the gills of freshwater adapted Chinese and shore crabs are able to overcome osmotic stresses in freshwater and seawater, respectively.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
shore crabs have developed an osmoregulatory strategy to absorb salt and water in a coupled way in order to maintain the osmotic equilibrium in the body fluids.
the crab gill is a good model to study the adaptation of epithelial ion transport mechanisms to environmental osmotic challenges.
freshwater adapted crabs use an active Na+-independent uptake of Cl−, whereas brackish water crabs use a coupled NaCl absorption.
The main takeaway from our work is that
crabs can adapt their gill epithelion to different environmental salinity by changing their transport mechanisms.
the freshwater crab gills are an excellent model system to study the cellular mechanisms of ion and water uptake and the molecular basis of osmoregulation in crustaceans.
the crab gill epithelum is an excellent preparation to study the mechanisms of NaCl absorption and secretion in marine and freshwater crabs.
